text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Pakistan and the International Monetary Fund have hammered out an agreement on all policy matters, paving the way for Islamabad to receive $80 million tranche of $600 million standby arrangement soon.
- Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto said her Pakistan People's Party will oppose any move to install a presidential form of government.
- The Field General Court Martial found four army officers accused of a coup conspiracy guilty of the charges shown against them and awarded them various terms of rigorous imprisonment.

- The State (central) Bank placed the recently-announced special foreign currency deposit scheme under the ambit of the rules governing permanent inflow of foreign currency funds. Most bankers say the move has made the scheme more realistic and estimate an inflow of $100-150 million by the end of November.
- Pakistan Telecommunication Co Ltd earned a record revenue of 7.2 billion rupees ($179 million) in the first quarter of 1996/97 (July-June) against 5.4 billion in the year-ago period.
- The government revised upwards the support prices of rice for 1996/97 crop to provide a fair return to growers.
- Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto will inaugurate the Aeronautical Communication and Control System at Karachi's Quaid-i-Azam International Airport today.
- The International Monetary Fund reached an agreement with Pakistan. "We are releasing the assistance of $160 million to Pakistan as fas as humanly possibly," an IMF official said.

- Ousted Punjab Chief Minister Manzoor Wattoo told the Lahore High Court he would not dissolve the provincial assembly if he was restored with full powers and given 60 days to seek a confidence vote. The court reserved its judgement in the case.
- Troops loyal to Afghan warlord General Abdul Rashid Dostum and former Herat governor Ismail Khan were poised for an attack on the Taleban-held western province of Herat.
